result.summary: This residential street features narrow sidewalks on both sides, which are occasionally obstructed by trash bins and building steps. The environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings, traffic calming measures, or physical buffers between the walkway and parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and building steps narrow the effective walking width on the left sidewalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits sight lines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crossings with high-visibility paint to designate safe pedestrian paths.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Introduce street trees to provide a psychological buffer from traffic and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous sidewalk and parallel on-street parking. While the walkway is clear, the lack of a buffer and the presence of parked vehicles create visual obstructions and a sense of exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow residential street with continuous sidewalks and parallel parking on both sides. While the street's narrow geometry likely limits vehicle speeds, the lack of marked crossings and significant visual obstructions from parked cars present risks to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars along both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway where cars are parked.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bags and bins placed on the sidewalk restrict the clear walking width.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to intersections to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential area.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street lined with brick row houses that front directly onto a concrete sidewalk. While a continuous walkway is provided, the environment lacks a dedicated furniture or planting zone, and parked vehicles are the only buffer between pedestrians and the travel lane.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb line obscure the visibility of pedestrians, particularly children, who might attempt to cross the street mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and along the curb line

hazards.name: Narrow Effective Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk is relatively narrow, and the presence of steps and occasional debris reduces the effective clear width for pedestrians passing one another.
